title: The Productivity Secret of Quincy Jones
author: Admired Leadership
summary: Written on the occasion of Quincy Jones's death, this article uses his career as a case study in single-tasking discipline. Rather than juggling multiple projects like many artists and executives, Jones committed to a father's early advice to never leave a task until it was done, working on one assignment at a time until it was fully complete before starting the next. The author contrasts this with the common creative habit of stepping away from a stuck project to seek fresh perspective, noting Jones instead pushed straight through resistance. The piece credits this singular focus, sustained across seven decades and 28 Grammy wins, as a major driver of his extraordinary output. It closes by suggesting readers apply the same one-task-at-a-time discipline to even a single task per day.

quotes: Few artists have been as commercially successful or prolific as Jones during his more than seven decades of musical influence.

Nothing is more satisfying than fully completing an important project or task.
